title: Docs: Route experiments customer guide + SDK notes + examples
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Context
- Route-level experiments (A/B/n) are rolling out in Console (Rollouts) and customers need a single canonical guide that covers: creating experiments, stickiness keys, variant attribution headers, reading metrics in Console, and safe operation/guardrails.
- This ticket owns customer-facing documentation + SDK integration notes + an example app. It also coordinates review with DevEx, Support, SRE, and Security to ensure we do not over-promise (esp. around statistical significance) and that troubleshooting guidance reflects real failure modes seen in beta.

Audience
- Platform/ML engineers implementing experiments in production.
- Application engineers who want a quick recipe for A/B testing two model variants behind a route.
- Support / Solutions Engineering (internal) using the guide for triage.

Deliverables
1) Customer guide (docs site)
- “Route experiments” overview and when to use it (vs canary rollouts).
- Create/start/stop lifecycle, including ramp strategy (1% -> 10% -> 50% etc.).
- Variant configuration: model selection, compatibility expectations, fallback interaction (high-level), and max variants guidance.
- Stickiness keys (deterministic assignment):
  - Recommended key precedence and what constitutes a stable key.
  - What happens when the key is missing (and how we mitigate skew).
  - Guidance for multi-tenant apps (avoid cross-tenant contamination).
- Attribution in responses:
  - Which headers/fields indicate assigned experiment + variant.
  - How to log them in the app for debugging and support.
- Metrics definitions surfaced in Console:
  - Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) definitions and caveats for streaming.
  - Error rate definition (which status codes count; how retries are treated at a high level).
  - Cost/token definitions (what we attribute; caveats).
  - Quality metric (if enabled): what it represents, sampling, and “not statistically significant” disclaimer.
- Guardrails & auto-stop:
  - Default guardrails vs custom thresholds.
  - Soft-stop semantics (GA promise) vs optional hard-stop (behind kill switch / enterprise config).
  - Clear “what happens when a guardrail triggers” and who gets notified.
- Troubleshooting section (must be practical):
  - Variant skew / unexpected allocation.
  - Missing attribution (common causes: streaming retries, missing headers, propagation lag).
  - Results dashboard appears stale (aggregation delay vs config propagation lag).
  - Cardinality pitfalls when tagging custom route IDs (route template vs raw path).

2) SDK notes
- TypeScript + Python: how to pass a stickiness key (and how to choose one).
- How to enable additional logging for variant assignment.
- How to read/interpret response headers / fields.
- Backwards compatibility and what happens if you do nothing (no stickiness key supplied).

3) Example app
- Minimal “two-variant” example showing:
  - stable stickiness key generation (per user/customer)
  - emitting logs with experiment_id/variant_id
  - verifying split distribution in local/staging
  - interpreting variant headers in responses

Non-goals / explicit caveats (must be in docs)
- We do not provide a full statistical significance engine in GA; Console shows deltas and guardrail thresholds.
- We do not accept customer-defined custom metrics ingestion in initial release; only Redwood-defined metrics + optional eval signals.
- Multi-region cross-population rebalancing is out of scope; assignment is deterministic given the stickiness key.

Source-of-truth references (for authorship consistency)
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/route-level-ab-testing-prd.json
- ADR-047 deterministic bucketing: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-047-deterministic-experiment-bucketing.json
- ADR-048 attribution schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-048-experiment-metrics-attribution-schema.json
- DX integration notes: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/route-experiments-integration-notes.json
- Audit requirements (for “what’s logged” section): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/experiment-config-audit-events.json

Acceptance criteria
- Docs page(s) published on docs site under Console/Rollouts with clear nav and search keywords (“A/B testing”, “experiments”, “route experiments”).
- Includes stickiness key guidance + a concrete recommended default for most customers.
- Includes a short “Troubleshooting: missing attribution” section that matches known beta issues and mitigations.
- Support reviewed: variant header interpretation is unambiguous and includes exact strings customers will see.
- SRE reviewed: guardrail semantics match what we actually ship (soft-stop in GA; hard-stop described as optional / controlled).
- SDK notes reviewed by DevEx maintainers (TS + Python) and aligned with shipped SDK behavior.
- Example app merged and referenced from docs.

Rollout notes
- Must be ready for beta expansion and again reviewed before GA enable-by-default.
- Keep copy consistent with Console UI terms: “Route experiments”, “Variants”, “Traffic split”, “Guardrails”, “Audit history”.

Implementation plan
- Draft outline + terminology alignment with Design (Kenji, Alicia) to match UI labels.
- Write guide + SDK notes + troubleshooting.
- Add cross-links to runbook-style internal docs where appropriate (internal-only links should be omitted from customer guide).
- Coordinate reviews (DevEx, Support, SRE, Security).
- Merge docs + examples; confirm docs build + link integrity; add release note snippet if needed.

Risks / watchouts
- Overpromising on “quality” metric: ensure disclaimers about sampling and non-significance.
- Confusion between canary rollouts and experiments: must clearly distinguish when each is appropriate and how they interact at a high level.
- Header naming stability: ensure docs reflect final header names and that SDKs surface them consistently.

Linked work
- Docs PR (customer guide): sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-1447-route-experiments-customer-guide.json
- Example app PR: sources/github/redwood-examples/pr-608-route-experiments-sample-app.json
- SDK PRs: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-533-add-experiment-sticky-key-option.json, sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-721-add-route-experiment-headers-support.json
comments: 2025-02-13 (Marissa Cole): Please make sure we clearly state GA scope: deltas + guardrails, no full stats-sig engine. Also, customers keep asking “is this the same as canaries?”—we need a crisp comparison section.

2025-02-18 (Dylan Brooks): Drafted outline + pulled terminology from UX spec so docs match Console. Next: confirm header names and stickiness key precedence with Jordan (ADR-047) and SDK behavior with DevEx.

2025-02-25 (Caleb Johnson): Telemetry caveat: streaming retries were missing attribution in early beta; fixed path is landing. Docs should include “If you see missing experiment_id on streaming, update to >= python sdk X / ts sdk Y and ensure you’re not stripping response headers at your gateway.”

2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Guardrails section: please avoid implying we always hard-stop in GA. Current plan is soft-stop + notification; hard-stop is optional behind a kill switch and only for severe regressions. Add language about verifying alerting + oncall ownership before enabling hard-stop.

2025-03-10 (Support relay via Dylan): Beta customer confusion: they didn’t know what the variant headers meant and assumed it was an error. Please include exact header names, example values, and a short tooltip-like explanation in docs.

2025-03-18 (Kenji Nakamura): UX alignment: use “Traffic split” (not “allocation”) in customer-facing copy. In advanced section you can mention allocation/eligibility rules. Also: add a note that stop is immediate from routing perspective, but dashboards can lag due to aggregation windows.

2025-03-27 (Dylan Brooks): Review complete with DevEx + Support + SRE. Docs PR updated: added stickiness key examples (customer_id/user_id), clarified missing-key behavior + skew risk, and expanded troubleshooting (stale results vs propagation lag). Example app merged and referenced.
2025-04-09 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done for console-2025.04 train. Confirmed docs are linked from release notes draft and Console “Learn more” points to the new guide.
